definitions.gloss: most important; of the highest importance; top priority
definitions.explanation: The superlative form of {重要|じゅうよう}, indicating something that is of the greatest significance or urgency among all options.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}が{最重要|さいじゅうよう}だ。
これは{最重要|さいじゅうよう}な{課題|かだい}として{取|と}り{組|く}むべきだ。
examples.english: We should tackle this as the most important issue.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}では{顧客|こきゃく}の{満足度|まんぞくど}を{最重要|さいじゅうよう}の{目標|もくひょう}に{掲|かか}げた。
examples.english: At the meeting, they set customer satisfaction as the top-priority goal.

notes:
Formed by the superlative prefix {最|さい} (most) + {重要|じゅうよう} (important). Used as a pre-noun modifier with な or directly before a noun without な in more formal/written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最重要|さいじゅうよう}{課題|かだい}: the most important issue
- {最重要|さいじゅうよう}{事項|じこう}: top-priority item
- {最重要|さいじゅうよう}{人物|じんぶつ}: the most important person
- {最重要|さいじゅうよう}{拠点|きょてん}: the most critical base/location

USAGE:
Often used with な when modifying a noun ({最重要|さいじゅうよう}な{問題|もんだい}), but in formal writing the な may be dropped ({最重要|さいじゅうよう}{問題|もんだい}). Can also be used as a predicate: Xが{最重要|さいじゅうよう}だ (X is the most important).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {重要|じゅうよう}: important (base form, without superlative)
- {最優先|さいゆうせん}: highest priority (emphasizes order of action rather than inherent importance)
- {肝心|かんじん}: crucial, essential (more colloquial, focuses on what matters most in a practical sense)
